subject.title: RFC: Org claim disputes and account recovery

question: Should the current namespace-claim intake and guarded publisher-recovery implementation be accepted as final policy, or should this RFC remain open until maintainers define the remaining disposition and private-evidence rules?
rationale: The remaining work is a trust-and-safety policy boundary, not a narrow source repair; automation cannot decide what proof is sufficient for transfers, reservations, quarantine, aliases, denials, or recovery exceptions.

options.title: Keep RFC Open For Synthesis
options.body: Maintain this issue as the canonical discussion until a maintainer/security synthesis records accepted policy, rejected alternatives, and any public docs or private runbook follow-up.

options.title: Accept Current Partial Policy
options.body: Treat the existing claim form, namespace guide, and publisher recovery tooling as sufficient final policy, then close with a maintainer statement explaining that case-by-case staff discretion is intentional.

options.title: Split Remaining Decisions
options.body: Open narrower follow-ups for deleted/inactive owner disposition and private evidence handling, then close this RFC as superseded by those tracked decisions.

recommendation.title: Keep RFC Open For Synthesis
recommendation.body: Maintain this issue as the canonical discussion until a maintainer/security synthesis records accepted policy, rejected alternatives, and any public docs or private runbook follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick authored the RFC and most current namespace/recovery surfaces, while CODEOWNERS already routes the security-sensitive files through secops review.
